overview: This file documents U.S. interdepartmental and Allied-occupation discussions concerning the authority and geographic jurisdiction of Japan’s newly created Maritime Safety Board. The first group of papers traces State and Army clearance of a U.S. response to French doubts about whether Japanese officers could stop and search foreign or Allied vessels in Japanese territorial waters, culminating in instructions to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission that the Board acted as an authorized agent of SCAP. A later despatch and its enclosures record a British objection to an erroneous English translation of the Maritime Safety Board Law that appeared to extend its jurisdiction to “the high seas adjacent to Japan,” followed by SCAP’s reply and the Japanese government’s published correction.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on French attitude toward the Japanese Maritime Safety Board
subfiles.about: Ray seeks Allison’s approval of a draft intended to reconcile differing views within the State Department about the French position on the Japanese Maritime Safety Board.
subfiles.summary: Ray circulates a draft memo reconciling views on France's objection to Japan's Maritime Safety Board.

subfiles.title: Memorandum proposing an information paper on the French coastal-patrol statement
subfiles.about: Ray recommends circulating a U.S. information paper instead of making an oral statement in response to the French declaration on Japanese coastal patrols.
subfiles.summary: Ray proposes an information paper answering France's public statement on Japan's coastal patrol authority.

subfiles.title: Draft instruction on the authority of the Japanese coastal patrol
subfiles.about: The draft states that Maritime Safety Board officers may stop and search foreign or Allied vessels in Japanese territorial waters as authorized agents of SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Draft argues Japan's Maritime Safety Board acts as SCAP's authorized agent under SCAPIN orders, letting it stop and search vessels in Japanese waters despite French objections.

subfiles.title: Army concurrence in the proposed response on Japanese coastal patrols
subfiles.from: W. H. Hault, for the Secretary of the Army
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention J. Franklin Ray Jr.
subfiles.about: The Department of the Army formally concurs in the draft memorandum to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Army concurs in the proposed response defending Japan's coastal-patrol authority against France's objection.

subfiles.title: Request for expedited Army clearance of the coastal-patrol position
subfiles.to: Colonel Lawler, Plans and Policy Group, Plans and Operations Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Ray asks Lawler to expedite Army review of the State Department’s draft position on the French coastal-patrol statement.
subfiles.summary: Ray requests expedited Army clearance of the draft position on Japan's coastal-patrol authority.

subfiles.title: Final instruction to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission on coastal patrols
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Saltzman directs the U.S. member to inform the Commission that the Maritime Safety Board acts under SCAP authority when stopping and searching vessels in Japanese territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Final instruction tells the US delegate to defend Japan's Maritime Safety Board as a lawful SCAP agent before the FEC.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 68 on correction of the Maritime Safety Board Law translation
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports correction of an English translation that incorrectly placed Maritime Safety Board authority on the high seas adjacent to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Despatch flags a mistranslation in Japan's Maritime Safety Board Law, later corrected in the Official Gazette.

subfiles.title: British note protesting the English translation of Article 1
subfiles.from: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The British mission asks that the Japanese government delete an unauthorized reference to the high seas from the English translation of the Maritime Safety Board Law.
subfiles.summary: Britain protests an English mistranslation suggesting Japan's patrol law covers the high seas, not just territorial waters.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply concerning correction of Article 1
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: SCAP headquarters informs the British mission that the Japanese government will publish a correction deleting the high-seas language.
subfiles.summary: SCAP confirms Japan will correct the mistranslated 'high seas' phrase in its patrol law's Official Gazette.

subfiles.title: Official Gazette erratum to the Maritime Safety Board Law
subfiles.from: Secretary of the Prime Minister’s Office
subfiles.about: The published erratum orders deletion of the words “on the High seas” from Article 1 of the Maritime Safety Board Law.
subfiles.summary: Gazette erratum deletes the wrongly translated 'high seas' phrase from Japan's Maritime Safety Board Law.

interest: Shows SCAP's legal basis for Japan's coastal patrol, and Britain's challenge to an erroneous high-seas translation.
